title: Idempotency claim result is discarded — handler falls through to find+transition on a duplicate (0-row) or claim-error
detail: All three claim branches yield Nil; Gleam has no early return, so a 0-row duplicate or claim-error falls through to find+mark. The claim gates nothing. The redelivery test passes only because find excludes the already-transitioned row.
recommended_fix: Nest find/mark/notify inside the Ok(Returned(_,[_,..])) arm so only a freshly-claimed event continues; have the 0-row and Error arms return Nil without falling through (or refactor with `use`).

title: notify_reference_awaiting_correction Result is discarded via ignore_result — failure is invisible (adjacent comment claims it's captured)
evidence:
// notification. Both are best-effort (a failure here is
              // captured but does not roll back the transition).
              write_audit(
                db,
                sentry,
                reference_call_id,
                source,
                terminal_reason,
              )
              case uuid.from_string(row.landlord_id) {
                Ok(landlord_id) ->
                  notification_dispatch.notify_reference_awaiting_correction(
                    db,
                    landlord_id,
                    reference_call_id,
                    row.contact_name,
                    row.applicant_full_name,
                  )
                  |> ignore_result
detail: ignore_result returns Nil for both Ok and Error, so a notification insert failure is never captured to Sentry. The 'captured' comment is false for this call (only write_audit captures); AC8's bell can silently never ring.
recommended_fix: Inspect the Result: on Error, call capture(...) (mirroring write_audit) before discarding, so a notification insert failure surfaces in Sentry like the audit failure does.
